intent: To demonstrate that decarbonizing the electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation sectors is the key to solving the majority of US carbon emission problems.

units.meaning: The four sectors named for decarbonization are Electricity generation, Residential, Commercial, and Transportation.

basis.note: Table value for Electricity generation; target sector.
Table value for Residential; target sector.
Table value for Commercial; target sector.
Table value for Transportation; target sector.

accepted_routes: Electricity generation, Residential, Commercial, and Transportation are the four target sectors.
The decarbonization set is electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation.
The four sectors highlighted are Electricity generation, Residential, Commercial, and Transportation.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Labels or highlights must distinguish these four sectors from the Industrial sector.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause naming 'electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation' should carry it.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify all four sectors in the decarbonization target set?

units.meaning: The four target sectors together total 82 percentage points: Electricity generation 28 + Residential 14 + Commercial 12 + Transportation 28. If normalized across all five listed percentages (sum 103), their share is about 80% (82/103≈79.6%).

basis.note: One of the four target sectors.
One of the four target sectors.
One of the four target sectors.
One of the four target sectors.

units.computation: 28+14+12+28=82; all five table values sum to 103, so 82/103≈79.6%.
accepted_routes: Electricity generation, Residential, Commercial, and Transportation together account for 82 percentage points.
Together these four sectors are about 80% of the five listed values if normalized (82/103≈79.6%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: A sum or combined annotation for the four target sectors must be visible or inferable from the highlighted slices.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause 'If electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation were mostly decarbonized' plus the 'solved a lot' conclusion.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the four-sector total as 82 percentage points (or ~80% normalized)?

units.meaning: Ranking by sector share: Transportation and Electricity generation are tied at 28% each; Industrial is 21%; Residential is 14%; Commercial is 12%.
accepted_routes: Transportation and Electricity generation are tied for largest at 28%, then Industrial 21%, Residential 14%, Commercial 12%.
The order is Transportation = Electricity generation (28%) > Industrial (21%) > Residential (14%) > Commercial (12%).
Commercial is smallest at 12%, followed by Residential at 14%.
Electricity generation and Transportation share the top share at 28% each.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Slice sizes and labels must show the tie at 28% and the descending order to 12%.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'broken down by economic sector' clause when the chart hierarchy is shown.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video convey the full sector ranking and the 28% tie, or only the four target sectors?

units.meaning: Industrial is the sector not included in the four-sector decarbonization target set; it is 21%.
accepted_routes: Industrial, at 21%, is the non-targeted sector.
The decarbonization set leaves out Industrial, which is 21%.
Industrial accounts for 21% and is not part of the four target sectors.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Industrial slice must be labeled 21% and visually not highlighted as one of the four targets.
units.temporal_anchor: The 'broken down by economic sector' clause or the moment the target set is contrasted with the remaining sector.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video identify Industrial as the excluded/non-target sector?

units.meaning: Electricity generation and Transportation together total 56 percentage points (28+28); normalized across all five listed values, they are about 54% (56/103≈54.4%).

basis.note: One of the two largest sectors.
One of the two largest sectors.

accepted_routes: Electricity generation plus Transportation equals 56 percentage points.
The two largest sectors together are 56%.
Together they are about 54% of the five listed values if normalized (56/103≈54.4%).
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both 28% slices or a combined annotation for them must be visible.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause listing electricity and transportation as target sectors.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state that the two largest sectors alone exceed half (if normalized) or total 56 percentage points?

optional_valid: The chart includes five economic sectors: Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Transportation, and Electricity generation.
Residential and Commercial together total 26 percentage points (14+12).
The four-sector target total (82) exceeds Industrial (21) by 61 percentage points (82-21=61).
Commercial is the smallest sector at 12%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that decarbonizing these sectors will reduce US carbon emissions by exactly 82%.
Stating the five table percentages sum to 100% (raw table sum is 103).
Extrapolating to future emissions, policy outcomes, or global emissions.
Presenting Industrial as part of the four-sector decarbonization target set.
Using a different denominator without stating the formula.
notes: Raw table percentages sum to 103, so normalized shares (e.g., 82/103≈79.6%) differ from raw percentage-point sums; use formulas when normalizing. The core intent is supported by the four-sector majority composition, not by a causal intervention estimate.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
